reason: The text describes the restoration of Joash to the throne under the leadership of Jehoiada the priest. While the text portrays Jehoiada instructing the commanders and officials, and giving orders (e.g., regarding guard duty and protecting the king), these are directives and organizational commands, not complaints about the people. In fact, the narrative shows the people responding positively—they rejoice ('וַיִּשְׂמַח כָּל־ עַם־ הָאָרֶץ'), support the establishment of the covenant, destroy the temple of Baal, and the city is at peace ('הָעִיר שָׁקָטָה'). The text contains no instance of Hebrew leaders complaining or expressing dissatisfaction with the people's conduct.
